key_insight: PIKS extends kernel methods to physics-informed learning with universal consistency for linear differential constraints, even when the true target is outside the RKHS.
engineering_relevance: It offers a closed-form, theoretically grounded alternative to PINNs for engineering problems with known differential physics, potentially improving reliability and interpretability.
method: Enforce linear differential operators directly in a kernel learning objective.
Use universal kernels such as Gaussian or Matérn to guarantee asymptotic learning.
Derive finite-sample error bounds via operator-theoretic analysis and source conditions.
evidence_signal: The paper reports numerical experiments showing PIKS is competitive with PINNs and traditional finite element methods.
watch_item: The finite-sample guarantees depend on suitable source conditions, so performance may still be sensitive to problem regularity and kernel choice.
